articles.body: The Shaheen political dynasty lives on in New Hampshire. Stefany Shaheen, the eldest daughter of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), won Tuesday’s hotly contested Democratic primary for the state’s 1st District, defeating Maura Sullivan and a host of other rivals despite facing attacks that she was leaning on her well-known surname. The seat, left open by Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas when he opted to run for Senate, is considered to be fairly competitive for the general election — former Vice President Kamala Harris won it by just two points in 2024. Shaheen attempted to create distance from her mother throughout her campaign, rebuking the deal the senator helped broker to end last fall’s government shutdown and leaning into her public service in Portsmouth and medical-research advocacy on the trail. Still, her family name helped her build an early polling lead and bank financial support . Nearly $740,000 raised by Shaheen’s campaign came from donors who had previously given to her mother — 39 percent of total itemized campaign dollars, according to a POLITICO analysis. One of those donors told POLITICO the senator reached out last fall seeking their support for her daughter. Sullivan, Shaheen’s main rival, attempted to weaponize the scion’s family ties in a year where the Democratic base has repeatedly spurned candidates with a perceived connection to the establishment. The primary grew acrimonious in its closing weeks as Shaheen and Sullivan tangled over campaign donations and aired attack ads as polls showed a tightening race. The contest also underwent a rapid winnowing toward the end as two candidates dropped out; one, progressive Christian Urrutia, endorsed Shaheen .
articles.headline: Stefany Shaheen, daughter of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, wins New Hampshire House primary

articles.body: A Republican-led bid to revive a redistricting plan that favors the GOP fell short at the Supreme Court Tuesday, but it later picked up steam after a federal judge in Missouri ruled that officials must move ahead with the districts used in primaries last month — a map that’s likely to net Republicans an additional House seat. Justice Brett Kavanaugh turned down a Republican-backed emergency appeal that sought to block a Missouri Supreme Court ruling last week restoring earlier district lines and ordering that voters to weigh in on the redistricting plan in November for use in future elections. However, Chief U.S. District Court Judge Stephen Clark, in a decision made public within minutes of Kavanaugh’s ruling, issued a temporary restraining order that effectively set aside the state Supreme Court’s decision and granted Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins’ request to move forward with the plan likely to elect a Republican in one of the state’s two districts currently held by Democrats. The Democratic group leading the push to block Republicans' redistricting efforts swiftly appealed Clark's decision to the 8th Circuit Court and asked the court for an emergency temporary stay while it considers the appeal. The group has asked Clark to stay his order, and it also asked Missouri's Supreme Court to hold Hoskins in contempt. The dissonant rulings add another layer of chaos to Missouri’s election administration. Local election officials had prepared for months as the debate over which map to use moved through the court system, planning for elections in the event either map gets used. The state used the new, gerrymandered map for August’s primaries. The timing of settling these legal disputes is crucial. The rulings came hours before the Tuesday deadline for Missouri election officials to make changes to any ballots, and ballots must be finalized before ballots begin to be sent out on Sept. 19. Hoskins sent an email to election officials Tuesday evening directing them to comply with Clark's order and prepare for November's election under the gerrymandered map, according to Democrats' filing Tuesday evening to the Missouri Supreme Court. Kavanaugh issued his ruling because he handles urgent matters arising in the 8th Circuit, which includes Missouri. Kavanaugh issued no explanation of his decision, nor did he indicate that he had referred the matter to the full court, as is customary in significant cases. Missouri officials could ask another justice for relief, but such requests are almost never granted. The justices rarely disturb state courts’ decisions about matters like the referendum petitions in Missouri that sought to put the redistricting before voters for approval. Clark, a St. Louis-based Trump appointee, said two Republican candidates who sued were likely to prevail in their arguments that changing the district lines at this point in the process would violate two provisions in the U.S. Constitution: one establishing the House of Representatives and another guaranteeing equal protection of the laws. Lawyers for state officials warned in their appeal to the Supreme Court that the state faced “disaster” and “unprecedented chaos” in part because primaries already took place under the new lines last month. Democrats argued any last-minute chaos to Missouri’s election administration was intentionally created by Hoskins, pointing to Republican leaders in the state arguing that delaying the decision on the redistricting referendum would benefit Republicans. President Donald Trump denounced the state Supreme Court ruling last week. “The Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America!" he wrote in a post on Truth Social . “Missouri must be able to use the map that was in effect just a couple of months ago, in the Primary. This is a Dark Day for “Justice” in Missouri!”
articles.headline: Missouri’s redistricting in flux after dissonant court rulings

articles.body: President Donald Trump will be at the center of this week’s GOP midterm convention. Many of his fellow Republicans are hoping he doesn’t make it all about him. The parade of lawmakers, candidates, donors and party officials now headed to Dallas for the two-day spectacle are counting on Trump to make a compelling pitch on the national stage before voters hit the polls. According to interviews with dozens of Republicans, they are largely hoping for a two-pronged approach aimed at getting the president’s committed supporters off the sidelines: a focus on what they call Democrats’ extreme positions and the accomplishments of the Republican Congress — most of which are now more than a year old. “Communism vs. common sense,” Rep. Riley Moore (R-W.Va.) said in an interview, calling the event a “scene-setter” that should stay laser-focused on “what’s on the line” for voters in the election. Republicans have reasons to be wary. Trump’s approval ratings are at record lows for his time in office, and many swing-district GOP lawmakers are torn between running from an unpopular president and alienating his base of committed supporters. There is little evidence Trump is content to let rank-and-file Republicans run away from him. The first pair of national midterm ads funded by his cash-rich political operation put Trump at the very center. One ad begins with businessman Dana White extolling Trump as “the toughest, most resilient person that I've ever met.” The other is more up congressional Republicans’ alley, with a Trump voiceover running through a litany of tax cuts included in last year’s “One Big Beautiful Bill.” Even if not all agree Trump is the party’s best spokesperson at this point, they are eager to see a new effort to promote the tax cuts, which were enacted in July 2025, and want to see them touted anew in Dallas. “It's incredibly important that we highlight what we've accomplished,” Rep. Derrick Van Orden (R-Wis.) said in an interview. “That's the perfect venue for that.” “It's a great opportunity for us to brag about what the Republican Party has done the last year and a half,” added Rep. Craig Goldman (R-Texas). “So certainly talking about the One Big Beautiful Bill.” While Van Orden and Goldman are attending the convention, which kicks off Wednesday and ends Thursday, many other lawmakers and candidates are staying back in their districts . Some of those Republicans said they have scheduling conflicts or simply want to campaign back home. But there are also qualms about Trump’s obsession with priorities that many of them consider off-message ahead of the midterms — such as pressuring Congress to take up the GOP elections bill known as the SAVE America Act. As GOP lawmakers begged Trump to get serious about tackling the high cost of living, the president has instead openly scoffed at “affordability” as an issue concocted by Democrats to hurt Republicans. He refused for months to help pass a major legislative package over the summer designed to help lower housing costs, and his trade wars and ongoing conflict with Iran have contributed to persistent inflation. A recent import deal designed to address rising beef prices came at the cost of upsetting American cattlemen. Speaker Mike Johnson brushed off a question last week about the risk of having candidates show up at a Trump-focused event given his disapproval ratings. “It was the president's idea, which is why he's getting credit for it, and it's rightfully so,” Johnson said. “I think it's going to be an extraordinary opportunity for us to get a couple of nights on national television to talk about our extraordinary record of achievement.” Other Republicans said the president was well positioned to send a message of “promises made, promises kept.” “Politics 101 is just telling folks what you're going to do, and then come to Washington and do it, and then go back and tell them what you did,” said Rep. Mark Harris (R-N.C.). “When you look at President Trump's agenda, securing the border, we've done that. That he wanted to make the tax cuts permanent, we've done that.” “Peace through strength — and I think we have moved in that direction,” he added. “Obviously, we got detoured to this journey over in Iran.” If there is one consensus message Republicans want the convention oriented around, it’s the choice between the legislative record Trump will be touting and a Democratic Party that they argue has moved way too far to the left — especially as progressive candidates, some of them democratic socialists, continue to win key primaries. Rep. Brian Jack (R-Ga.), a deputy chair of the House GOP campaign arm, said “you're going to see on full display each night a contrast that we've never seen before in politics.” “You've got Republicans that are campaigning on commonsense ideas. You've got Democrats that are being drawn to the absolute most extreme left of their party,” he said. “So I expect each night to see that on full display.” RNC national press secretary Natalie Baldassarre also said in a statement that the event would “put front and center Democrats' desire to abolish police and prisons, raise costs, and strip away our freedoms,” while also promoting “Republicans’ historic achievements.” “The Democratic Party has taken a turn for the worse recently,” added Rep. Nick LaLota (R-N.Y.), who is in a competitive race and not attending the convention. “America needs to be quite aware of that as they make their decision here in November.” LaLota is just one of scores of Republican members who are choosing not to travel to the convention — which has a price tag of $25,000 and up for lawmakers attending — but who have an interest in how the event goes off and what impression it gives voters. Rep. Morgan Griffith (R-Va.) called the midterm convention — the first held since Democrats did them in the late 1970s and early 1980s — “an interesting concept” and said he would be paying close attention to the size of the television audience. But he said he would be back in his safe red district campaigning. “I'm going to look forward to listening to it on the radio as I'm driving down the road, going from one spot in my district to another,” he said. Jordain Carney and Meredith Lee Hill contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Republicans are hoping ‘Trump-a-palooza’ isn’t only about Trump

articles.body: LAS VEGAS — If California Gov. Gavin Newsom runs for president in 2028, next-door Nevada will be a crucial test. This fall’s governor’s race is offering a preview. As GOP Gov. Joe Lombardo runs for reelection, he’s trying to pin high Nevada fuel prices — a majority of which is imported from California — on “Gavin Newsom’s energy policies.” He lambasts California as too expensive and too regulated . And he’s hammering his Democratic opponent, Attorney General Aaron Ford, for accepting Newsom’s endorsement , betting that it will turn off Nevada swing voters. “The contrast is simple: I'm fighting Gavin Newsom's agenda and Aaron Ford is trying to import it into Nevada,” Lombardo said in a statement to POLITICO. This could be a test run for 2028, when Newsom may call upon Nevadans — one-fifth of whom were born in California — to deliver him a primary victory in the early-voting state, and possibly a presidential victory. “They understand California costs more,” Donna West, chair of the Nevada Democratic Party’s senior caucus, said of Nevada’s California expats. “They also understand that California is the fourth-largest economy in the entire world, and that Gavin Newsom ran that as effectively as he possibly can.” Newsom’s office declined to comment. A person close to the governor, granted anonymity to discuss the sentiment in his orbit, said they are “thrilled” Republicans are spending money to “plaster Newsom’s name across a key early state.” “Republicans seem awfully concerned about an endorsement from someone who leads the 2028 Democratic field in Nevada by nearly 2-to-1,” the person said, pointing to a November 2025 Emerson poll of a hypothetical 2028 Democratic primary field. Ford, for his part, shrugs off the attacks. “Lombardo tries to cast blame elsewhere, but everyone knows that when the war started in February, that we saw our gas prices increase almost immediately,” Ford told POLITICO after a recent town hall in Las Vegas. “People believe their own eyes, and they remember their experiences.” The demonization of California is nothing new in Nevada politics: For years, Republicans have blasted their western neighbor as too expensive and too woke. But the stakes are higher, and the connection more palpable, this year, as Newsom explores a presidential bid. He would likely need to perform very well in Nevada, now second on the Democratic calendar, to build early momentum toward the party nomination. And come November 2028, he’d need to fare well in Nevada again, this time among the state’s general electorate, a plurality of which are independents. Newsom has stumped for Democrats across the country this cycle, and he blitzed through the South this week, including a swing through South Carolina, whose Democrats will vote first, right before Nevada, in 2028. But Republicans are looking to weaponize Newsom’s Silver State swing in July, where Ford introduced him at a new Las Vegas field office as “the governor of the great state of California.” “Our next president!” an audience member shouted, eliciting cheers. The Lombardo-aligned Better Nevada PAC shared polling with POLITICO in July showing Newsom’s favorability 20 points underwater in Nevada and losing a hypothetical 2028 head-to-head with Vice President JD Vance. Shortly thereafter, the PAC began an ad blitz tying Ford to the California governor. Billboards touting Newsom’s endorsement of Ford, paid for by the PAC, now line highways across Nevada , and digital and streaming ads have run consistently since the visit. “Newsom and Ford: Shared vision. Shared values,” one ad says . A person familiar with the PAC’s internal polling, granted anonymity to discuss private data, said it shows Newsom’s endorsement is now the second-most-known datapoint about the attorney general. “Gavin Newsom is the singular most unpopular elected official in Nevada,” said Jeremy Hughes, a longtime Nevada GOP strategist running the Lombardo-aligned PAC. “Aaron Ford brought him into the state. … There's no better way to help him out than to put up these signs and run ads, letting people know that he's excited about being endorsed by Gavin Newsom.” Republicans in the state have long blamed Californian expats for housing shortages and rising prices and connect their opponents to California liberals. A surge of ex-Californians leaving the state during the Covid-19 pandemic, some fleeing high taxes and cost of living , accelerated the trend. Sam Brown, the GOP nominee for U.S. Senate in 2024, blasted the “energy policies of Gavin Newsom”; in 2018, GOP governor nominee Adam Laxalt lamented the “Californization” of Nevada, even as Californians bankrolled his campaign . During Lombardo’s first run for governor in 2022, he slammed incumbent Democratic Gov. Steve Sisolak for taking his cues from Newsom. “Don’t let Steve Sisolak turn Nevada into California,” one post from his campaign read . Republicans tied their opponents to Nancy Pelosi for decades. Lombardo’s argument this time around is more focused. He notes that the vast majority of Nevada’s gasoline comes from California, and argues that California’s efforts to cut carbon emissions have caused fuel prices to soar. A gallon of gas in Nevada costs nearly $5, according to AAA , one of the highest prices in the nation. “The policies coming from Gavin Newsom and California Democrats … don't stop at their state line,” Lombardo said in a statement. “Nevada and other states import a significant portion of our fuel from California, so when Governor Newsom shuts down refineries and imposes regulations that reduce supply and increase costs, Nevada families feel the consequences at the pump.” It’s a strategy that allows Lombardo — running in a difficult national environment for incumbent Republicans — to acknowledge voters’ economic pain without blaming President Donald Trump or his own party. Indeed, Lombardo shared an April column in the Nevada Independent that placed blame at the feet of both Newsom and Trump. (Lombardo, in his post , blamed only Newsom.) Democrats don’t think voters will buy it. ‘“As far as gas prices, it's so obviously increased since the war,” Rep. Dina Titus said. “People in Nevada aren't stupid.” Ford has his own millstone to saddle Lombardo with: the president. At a recent town hall in Las Vegas, he repeatedly blasted the “Lombardo-Trump economy” that is “making everything too expensive.” “Voters absolutely tie the handling of the economy to Trump,” said Mike Noble, an independent Phoenix-based pollster who works in Nevada regularly. “Instead of blaming Trump, why not tie it to the boogeyman next door and blame California?” CORRECTION: An earlier version of this article misstated the year Sam Brown was the GOP nominee for Senate.

articles.body: Hi ha paraules que ens protegeixen de tota mena d’elements de la intempèrie, aixopluc n’és una . Ens poden resguardar d’un patac d’aigua, del fred, d’una ventada i, fins i tot… de la soledat. Buscant l’ aixopluc Hem buscat l’origen d’ aixopluc  i tots els camins conflueixen en el mateix punt, no hi ha controvèrsia. El lingüista Joan Coromines, al seu diccionari etimològic, explica l’origen d’ aixopluc  a l’entrada del seu pare,  aixoplugar .   Segons el lingüista, aixoplugar —o aixoplugar-se— prové del sinònim aixoplujar-se , que clarament podem veure d’on deriva: ‘Aixopluc’, origen “AIXOPLUGAR o aixoplugar-se, tret del sinònim soplujar-se i de la seva variant aixoplujar-se —derivat de pluja — per influència del català occidental esplugar-se , que vol dir el mateix i és derivat de ESPLUGA ‘gran caverna que sovint serveix d’aixopluc’, del llatí SPELUNCA.” Joan Coromines, ‘DECat’ La pluja va fer créixer aixopluc Veiem que Coromines traça aquí un doble camí: d’una banda, aixoplugar té com a parents propers soplujar-se i aixoplujar-se , formats clarament per pluja ; però, de l’altra, fa remuntar tota aquesta colla de mots a esplugar-se , derivat d’ espluga , que vol dir ‘ cova ’. Així doncs, una sola paraula recull dos sentits clau, pluja i cova . A Catalunya tenim pobles que contenen el nom d’ espluga , que fa referència a la presència de coves; és el cas de l’Espluga de Francolí, que té la Cova de la Font Major, ocupada durant la prehistòria. Aixopluc  ha estat la vuitena paraula escollida pel programa  Catakrac , de betevé, per preguntar a la mainada què creuen que vol dir. Descobreix les seves  respostes enginyoses, aquí!    També et pot interessar Paraules a la vista: aixopluc Catakrac agenda 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: Aquest 11 de setembre torna la Grossa de la Diada 2026 , una de les cites més esperades per miles de catalans. Com cada any, aquest sorteig especial de Loteries de Catalunya ofereix premis importants. T’expliquem quan es fa el sorteig, on pots comprar els números, quins són els premis que pots guanyar i també on podràs comprovar el teu número de la Grossa . Quan se celebra la Grossa de la Diada 2026? Com és habitual, el sorteig es fa l’ 11 de setembre del 2026 a les 13 h aproximadament, coincidint amb la Diada Nacional de Catalunya. També et pot interessar Diada 2026 a Catalunya i manifestació de l’11 de setembre a Barcelona: recorregut i horaris Jessica Moreno Cusac 2 minuts de lectura On comprovar els premis de la Grossa de la Diada 2026 El sorteig de la Grossa de la Diada no es televisa. Ara bé, com és habitual, a betevé publicarem els números premiats tan bon punt surtin del bombo. Si et preguntes com comprovar si has guanyat algun premi de la Grossa de la Diada del 2026 , a betevé t’ho posarem fàcil: pots consultar si tens una participació premiada amb el nostre comprovador . Es tracta d’una eina on hauràs d’introduir el número del teu bitllet, la sèrie i la quantitat jugada. Automàticament, et direm si has guanyat algun premi i, en cas afirmatiu, amb quants diners has estat afortunat. Molta sort! Quins premis hi ha per la Grossa de la Diada? Aquest any es posen a la venda 70.000 números (del 00000 al 69999), amb 35 sèries per número,  15 en format paper i 20 que els punts de venda poden imprimir directament. El preu per bitllet és de  5 € . El premi extraordinari és de 2.000.000 € per al bitllet que encerti tant el mateix número com la sèrie. Si coincideixen les cinc xifres del primer premi , però no la sèrie, el jugador rebrà 50.000 € . El segon premi serà de 20.000 €; el tercer , de 10.000 €, i el quart (segon reintegrament), de 5 € . Ara bé, tingues en compte que les terminacions i els números anteriors o posteriors també són premiats . articles.body: (ACN) L’actor, dramaturg i poeta Manel Dueso va morir aquest dimarts a la tarda als 73 anys a l’Hospital de Sant Pau. Nascut a Sabadell el 1953, es va llicenciar en interpretació a l’ Institut del Teatre de Barcelona i sempre va ser autodidacte com a director i autor teatral . Com a actor i director, va representar i dirigir més de 100 obres d’autors com ara Shakespeare, Molière, Txékhov, Tennessee Williams, Beckett, Fassbinder i Genet, entre d’altres. També va treballar al cinema i la televisió com a director d’interpretació, guionista i actor . Va ser fundador de la Sala Beckett . Precisament, la temporada passada va estrenar l’obra Jambo bwana al Teatre Nacional de Catalunya . També et pot interessar Sergi Belbel, Victoria Szpunberg i Oriol Pla encapçalen la temporada 2026/27 de la Sala Beckett Josep T. París 3 minuts de lectura Obra literària Com a escriptor, és autor de més de 20 espectacles . Premi de Teatre dels Premis Literaris Ciutat de València 2023, Dueso va publicar tres llibres: les peces teatrals Mata’m (Lapislàtzuli, 2023) i L’encant de les nenes (Bromera, 2024) i el recent poemari Som cavalls d’escuma en camps de menta (Lapislàtzuli, 2026), recitat amb els actors Francesc Orella i Montse German i amb la pianista Bárbara Granados al Q-ars Teatre i a la Sala la Planeta, entre altres espais.

articles.body: La medalla de la presidència de la Generalitat de Catalunya és un símbol que està present durant la presa de possessió d’aquest càrrec. Jaume Mercadé , joier i net del pintor i joier Jaume Mercadé i Queralt, explica al Va passar aquí que aquesta obra d’orfebreria la va dissenyar el seu avi el 1932 al taller de la botiga situada al passeig de Gràcia 46 . L’exili del medalló Mercadé assenyala que el seu avi va rebre l’encàrrec del president de la Generalitat, Francesc Macià , a través del seu conseller de Cultura, Ventura Gassol , de fer el projecte de la medalla d’aquesta institució. “Va fer un disseny tipus art-déco, que era el que aplicava a les seves joies”, apunta Mercadé. A partir d’aquí va ser aprovat per la Generalitat i Mercadé va dur a terme l’execució de la peça amb els seus operaris. El medalló el va estrenar el president Francesc Macià i quan va morir va passar al president, Lluís Companys , que va marxar amb la joia a l’exili. Un cop a França, Companys va posar el medalló a la caixa forta d’una entitat bancària . El 1977 , quan s’instaura la Generalitat provisional, el president Josep Tarradellas demana que es pagui el rescat de la medalla. Quan el president espanyol intenta posar-li la medalla a Tarradellas no se’n surt, perquè no saben com funciona la tanca, i el president de la Generalitat l’acaba agafant amb les mans. També et pot interessar La història de la noia del mocador i Lluís Companys Gabriela Grífol Porta 1 minut de lectura Un símbol de 12 presidents Jaume Mercadé recorda que quan el president Jordi Pujol va arribar a la presidència del Palau de la Generalitat el van cridar perquè es fes càrrec de la restauració del medalló. La joia “estava molt malament” , assegura Mercadé. Dels 12 presidents que ha tingut la Generalitat des de la República, 10 s’han penjat la medalla de la presidència. Un va optar per posar-la sobre un domàs vermell durant la presa de possessió. “L’altre va ser a l’exili, que va prendre possessió”, assenyala Mercadé, “però d’una manera no oficial”. El medalló fa 167 grams d’or de 18 quirats , amb quatre pedres de quars d’ònix rectangulars als cantons i té un cordó de malla tubular. articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) El director general dels Mossos d’Esquadra , Josep Lluís Trapero , ha presentat aquest dimecres la dimissió com a director general de la Policia després de dos anys en el càrrec, segons ha avançat La Vanguardia i ha confirmat el Departament d’Interior. Precisament, la consellera d’Interior, Núria Parlon , ha convocat aquest dimecres la prefectura per comunicar els canvis que es produiran en l’organigrama , tenint en compte que el comissari en cap, Miquel Esquius , es jubila. També et pot interessar Parlon confirma Trapero com a director dels Mossos d’Esquadra Redacció 3 minuts de lectura El Departament d’Interior ha confirmat que Ferran López serà el director de la Policia —també destacat per ser mediador en el procés i que ara forma part de la prefectura— i continuarà el llegat a partir del 15 de setembre. Pel que fa al càrrec de Miquel Esquius, ha anunciat que el relleu serà Sílvia Catà . Fins ara, Catà era comissària de la Regió Policial de Girona i serà la primera dona a ocupar aquest càrrec . Deixa el càrrec per voluntat pròpia Interior afirma que Trapero deixa el càrrec per voluntat pròpia després d’aquests dos anys. Per això, Parlon li agraeix la tasca desenvolupada, així com la vocació de servei públic. De fet, a la compareixença ha deixat clar que ha estat una decisió “personal i irrevocable” , i també ha assegurat que la relació entre el Departament i els Mossos ha estat bona durant aquests anys. Així, no creu que les discrepàncies que han sorgit en aquesta etapa “siguin les que han portat a la decisió”. Ha insistit que només hi ha “ paraules d’agraïment ” cap a Trapero i Esquius, i que ara “ els llistons estan alts “. Ara bé, Trapero no marxarà del tot, ja que continuarà ocupant un càrrec a la Comissaria d’Avaluació i està previst que formi part de la Prefectura. Aposta per la feminització del cos Amb Catà com a nova comissària en cap, han sorgit els dubtes sobre si ara s’apostarà per una feminització del cos . Segons Parlon, “podria haver estat també un comissari”, però és conscient que el nou nom té una rellevància simbòlica . De fet, ha recordat que la feminització del cos està impregnant i que en la propera promoció el percentatge de dones ja supera el 40 %: “La idea és assemblar-se el més possible a la societat”. articles.body: La pluja és la protagonista d’aquest dimecres a part de Catalunya , sobretot a l’àrea metropolitana de Barcelona i altres punts del litoral i del prelitoral. articles.body: Barcelona i l’àrea metropolitana estan en alerta màxima aquest dimecres per la previsió d’ un episodi de pluges torrencials . De moment la pluja ha passat de llarg a la ciutat, i la possibilitat que ho faci amb intensitat també s’allunya. Tot i això, s’han registrat retards en diverses línies de Rodalies , un llamp ha obligat a suspendre l’alta velocitat entre Madrid i Barcelona i s’han cancel·lat una trentena de vols a l’aeroport de Barcelona-El Prat. De manera preventiva, la Generalitat ha cancel·lat les classes, l’activitat sanitària no urgent a 5 comarques del litoral i prelitoral barcelonès. Són el Vallès Occidental, el Baix Llobregat, el Garraf, i l’Alt i el Baix Penedès. En aquesta pàgina pots seguir minut a minut l’evolució d’aquest episodi de fortes precipitacions i risc d’inundacions a l’àrea de Barcelona. Malgrat que la situació meteorològica és d’alta complexitat i es fa difícil preveure exactament on acabarà descarregant amb més energia, els ingredients perquè es produeixin veritables patacs d’aigua hi són ben presents : aire fred en altura, humitat a tots els nivells, molta energia acumulada en superfície i un mar molt més calent de l’habitual. Les precipitacions s’estendran posteriorment cap a la plana vallesana i el litoral barceloní i el Maresme. articles.body: Et preguntes quin recorregut farà la manifestació de la Diada 2026 a Barcelona ? Com ja és habitual, diverses entitats independentistes convoquen una marxa, que és un dels actes més multitudinaris de l’ 11 de setembre a Barcelona . L’ANC, Òmniuc Cultural, l’AMI, el Consell de la República, la Intesindical i el CIEMEN han convocat una jornada de mobilització descentralitzada, amb marxes a Barcelona, Amposta i Girona. Aquest any l’independentisme sortirà al carrer sota el lema “ Aquest 11-S, hi soc, hi som. Independència ” i articularà la mobilització en dues columnes que representaran el present i el futur de Catalunya en qüestions com els drets socials. Segons l’ANC, “Catalunya viu un moment de malestar compartit amb problemes als serveis públics (educació, sanitat, col·lapse de Rodalies), l’emergència lingüística, la crisi de l’habitatge, les dificultats de la pagesia o un model econòmic fallit”. En contraposició, els convocants aposten per la independència com a “única eina per construir un futur millor”. articles.body: La pluja intensa i el risc d’inundacions d’aquest dimecres poden condicionar la mobilitat dels treballadors per anar als llocs de treball a l’àrea de Barcelona. Per això, la Generalitat ha recomanat fer teletreball en aquelles feines no essencials i ha demanat no fer desplaçaments en cotxe que no siguin necessaris. Unes mesures que afecten directament la rutina laboral diària dels treballadors a la ciutat de Barcelona i l’entorn metropolità També et pot interessar Classes suspeses i teletreball: en alerta per pluges fortes al litoral i prelitoral sud metropolità Lluís Cruz Berasategui 3 minuts de lectura Absència remunerada per força major Per tot això, el sindicat UGT ha demanat a totes les empreses que apliquin l’article 37.3 G de l’Estatut dels treballadors per protegir el personal laboral afectat per l’alerta de pluja excepcional prevista aquest dimecres. L’article reconeix a tothom el permís a absentar-se del lloc de feina , amb dret a remuneració, quan hi hagi situacions de força major derivades de riscos greus i imminents, com és el cas d’aquest episodi meteorològic. També et pot interessar S’acosta un gran canvi de temps: baixada potent de la temperatura acompanyada de tempestes fortes Jordi Montserrat 2 minuts de lectura Obligació de les empreses En un comunicat, la UGT considera que la seguretat i la salut dels treballadors és una prioritat absoluta en aquest context d’intensitat de pluja i inundacions. La formació recorda que les empreses tenen l’obligació legal de garantir la protecció de les plantilles, facilitant el treball a distància sempre que sigui viable i evitant exposar els treballadors a riscos innecessaris. També et pot interessar Què hem de fer els treballadors quan hi ha alertes de Protecció Civil i tanquen les escoles? Olga Borràs Boada 2 minuts de lectura Les universitats, en alerta La Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF) no tancarà els campus de Barcelona, tot i que ha demanat a estudiants i professorat que provinguin de les comarques afectades pel risc de pluja torrencial que evitin qualsevol desplaçament que no sigui estrictament necessari. Per la seva banda, la Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB ) ha suspès l’activitat al campus de Bellaterra, al campus de Sabadell i a la Unitat Docent Parc Taulí, d’acord amb la decisió del govern de suspendre l’activitat universitària al Vallès Occidental.
